chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who visits the House (Kaaba) before shaving [his head], he said: It is not appropriate unless he is forgetful.

Then he said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came to him some people on the Day of Sacrifice, and some of them said: O Messenger of Allah, I shaved before I sacrificed, and some of them said: I shaved before I threw [the pebbles]. They did not leave anything that it was appropriate for them to delay except that they hastened it, so he said: There is no blame.

key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim shaves his head before sacrificing or throwing pebbles during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the fiqh of Hajj ritual sequencing (tartib), distinguishing between the ideal order and the ruling for those who hasten actions due to forgetfulness or necessity. It leverages the Prophetic precedent of the 'People of Qada' who performed rituals out of sequence to establish the principle of 'la haraj' (no blame), reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease in worship when the core obligations are fulfilled. This ruling underscores the flexibility within the strictures of Hajj, prioritizing the completion of rites over rigid chronological perfection in cases of genuine error.
